_meta.source: enemy/group_<set>.rel — DSIF; the wave table is 12-byte {ptr, count, flag} records, ptr -> count u32 enemy ids
_meta.located_structurally: the root struct layout DIFFERS per file — .P.P.... for d, P...P.P. for f1, .P...... for f3 and f4 — so reading the table pointer from a fixed root word only works for group_d. That is why an earlier pass got 1 template for f1. The table is now found by scanning every relocation target for 12-byte records whose ptr advances by exactly count*4, which needs no assumption about the root at all.
_meta.validated: all five waves kion observed in valley still match group_d: A2 wave 1 and C1 wave 1 -> template 3, A2 wave 2 -> template 2, C4 wave 2 -> template 0, C3 -> template 10.
_meta.sets_are_nearly_identical: every set draws from the same enemy pool (63 distinct ids, 67 for f1) with the same maximum id of 68 and almost the same size distribution. So the set does NOT meaningfully change which waves exist — f1 through f4 are not difficulty tiers in their template lists. Whatever differs per set must be in the per-room-code table that ASSIGNS templates, not in the templates themselves.
_meta.group_2nd: 608 bytes with 19 relocations and no wave table — a different kind of file, not decoded
